paper: ai-and-society/The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity. Evidence from GitHub Copilot
reason: GitHub Copilot is a coding agent/tool for developers; the paper evaluates an LLM agent's impact on task completion and career entry support.
summary: GitHub Copilot enables developers to complete HTTP server implementation 55.8% faster, with heterogenous effects suggesting promise for supporting career transitions into software development.

paper: data-centric-ml/augmentation-and-synthetic-data/Fake it till you make it. Learning transferable representations from synthetic ImageNet clones
reason: Focuses on using synthetic data from generative models to replace real training data; core contribution is about synthetic training data effectiveness rather than diffusion model capabilities.
summary: Stable Diffusion-generated ImageNet clones trained from class names alone close the gap with real images for classification, and models trained on synthetic data match real-data-trained models on transfer tasks.

paper: data-centric-ml/data-quality-and-shift/Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet
reason: Dataset shift evaluation: new test sets reveal models' generalization failures to harder examples, not test-set overfitting
summary: ImageNet and CIFAR-10 classifiers drop 11–14% and 3–15% accuracy respectively on new test sets built to original creation procedures, driven by poor generalization to harder image distributions rather than adaptive overfitting.

paper: data-centric-ml/labels-and-annotation/The Perspectivist Paradigm Shift. Assumptions and Challenges of Capturing Human Labels
reason: The paper examines annotation practices and how to handle disagreement between annotators—a core labeling quality and methodology issue.
summary: Perspectivist approaches treat annotator disagreement as information-rich rather than noise, challenging longstanding label aggregation assumptions and requiring new data labeling practices.

paper: data-centric-ml/weak-supervision/Snorkel. Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision
reason: Foundational weak supervision system for programmatic labeling.
summary: Snorkel denoises labeling functions via data programming, enabling 2.8× faster model training and within 3.60% performance of hand-curated datasets.

paper: deep-learning/A continual learning survey. Defying forgetting in classification tasks
reason: Surveys continual learning methods for sequential task acquisition without catastrophic forgetting—a fundamental deep learning training paradigm.
summary: Framework for the stability-plasticity trade-off in continual learning; empirical comparison of 11 methods on Tiny ImageNet and iNaturalist.

paper: deep-learning/architectures/Going Deeper with Convolutions
reason: Inception is a foundational CNN architecture contributing multi-scale processing design principles for deep networks; evaluated on vision tasks but the contribution is at the architectural level.
summary: Inception blocks combine multi-scale convolutions in parallel, achieving ImageNet ILSVRC'14 state-of-the-art with 22-layer GoogLeNet using constant computational budget.

paper: deep-learning/efficiency-and-compression/Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
reason: BERT-era pretrained encoder fine-tuning and adaptation for downstream NLU tasks
summary: Knowledge distillation from BERT into single-layer BiLSTM networks matches ELMo performance across paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification with 100× fewer parameters and 15× faster inference.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/ab-testing/Trustworthy online controlled experiments. five puzzling outcomes explained
reason: Directly addresses controlled experiments at scale, their pitfalls, and trustworthy analysis — the exact scope of the ab-testing folder
summary: Analysis of puzzling outcomes in thousands of online controlled experiments reveals root causes across OEC, click tracking, effect trends, experiment length, power, and carryover effects.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/causal-inference/A Large Scale Benchmark for Individual Treatment Effect Prediction and Uplift Modeling
reason: Uplift modeling and Individual Treatment Effect prediction are core causal inference problems; this paper explicitly addresses uplift at scale using RCT data.
summary: Benchmark of 13.9M RCT samples (210x prior scale) enables statistical evaluation of Individual Treatment Effect and uplift prediction methods.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/metric-design/Deconfounding User Satisfaction Estimation from Response Rate Bias
reason: User satisfaction measurement and deconfounding from confounding factors; user satisfaction explicitly mentioned in this folder's scope
summary: Multi-task learning jointly predicting response rate and satisfaction deconfounds satisfaction models from selection bias where respondents are likelier to report higher ratings.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/variance-reduction/Consistent Transformation of Ratio Metrics for Efficient Online Controlled Experiments
reason: Proposes sensitivity-improvement techniques for ratio metrics in A/B testing, extending variance-reduction methods to ratio-level criteria.
summary: Ratio transformation: converts ratio metrics to user-level equivalents to enable variance-reduction techniques while preserving directionality and significance level, achieving +34% sensitivity improvement.

paper: generative-models/gans-and-vaes/Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and Super-Resolution
reason: Style transfer and super-resolution are established computer vision tasks and applications.
summary: Perceptual losses from pretrained networks enable 1000× faster style transfer than optimization methods with comparable quality, and improve super-resolution over per-pixel losses.

paper: graphs/graph-embeddings/Fast and Accurate Network Embeddings via Very Sparse Random Projection
reason: FastRP is a random-projection-based node embedding method; the folder explicitly lists it in scope alongside DeepWalk and node2vec, which are its baselines.
summary: Very sparse random projection learns node embeddings 4,000× faster than DeepWalk and node2vec with comparable or better performance.

paper: graphs/graph-neural-networks/A Comprehensive Survey on Graph Neural Networks
reason: Comprehensive survey of GNN architectures and types, explicitly covered by the folder scope
summary: Taxonomy of graph neural networks into four categories—recurrent, convolutional, autoencoders, spatial-temporal—with applications across domains and benchmark evaluation.

paper: interpretability/explainability/Grad-CAM. Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
reason: Visual saliency-based feature attribution technique for explaining CNN decisions through gradient-derived localization maps.
summary: Gradient-weighted class activation mapping uses backpropagated gradients to localize important image regions explaining CNN predictions across diverse architectures for classification, captioning, and VQA without retraining.

paper: interpretability/mechanistic/Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
reason: The paper introduces a method for circuit analysis—finding sparse computational subgraphs—and interpretable feature decomposition in language model MLPs, which is the core scope of mechanistic interpretability.
summary: Transcoders approximate dense MLP layers with sparse ones for weights-based circuit analysis, factorizing model computations into interpretable input-dependent and input-invariant terms.

paper: llm/agents/Reflexion. Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
reason: Core contribution is improving language agent learning through reinforcement via linguistic feedback and episodic memory, without weight updates.
summary: Episodic memory of reflected feedback improves agent decisions, reaching 91% pass@1 on HumanEval without weight updates.

paper: llm/architecture/Byte Latent Transformer. Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
reason: Byte-level transformer architecture variant, exactly matching the tokenization and byte-level models scope in the folder description.
summary: Byte-level transformer with entropy-allocated patches matches tokenization performance while demonstrating significantly better scaling for fixed inference costs.

paper: llm/architecture/efficient-attention-and-long-context/Efficient Attention. Attention with Linear Complexities
reason: Proposes linear-complexity attention mechanism, directly matching the scope of efficient attention variants alongside Longformer and Reformer.
summary: Linear-complexity attention mechanism equivalent to dot-product attention achieves state-of-the-art stereo depth estimation on Scene Flow.

paper: llm/architecture/recurrent-and-state-space/RWKV. Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
reason: RWKV is a linear attention RNN-Transformer hybrid explicitly listed in this folder's scope.
summary: Linear attention enables RWKV to train like a Transformer and infer like an RNN, matching Transformer performance at 14 billion parameters.

paper: llm/context/Retrieval meets Long Context Large Language Models
reason: Evaluates retrieval-augmented generation versus context window extension and demonstrates their combination for optimal long-context performance.
summary: Retrieval-augmented Llama2-70B-32K beats GPT-3.5-turbo-16k on long-context QA and few-shot tasks; retrieval augmentation on 4K context achieves parity with 16K-context finetuned models while being faster.

paper: llm/efficiency/LLM Pruning and Distillation in Practice. The Minitron Approach
reason: The paper applies pruning and distillation (both explicitly mentioned in this folder's scope) to create smaller LLMs, with the core contribution being how to apply these techniques effectively with restricted dataset access.
summary: Teacher fine-tuning on target data before distillation compresses Mistral NeMo 12B to 8B and Llama 3.1 8B to 4B via structured pruning.

paper: llm/evaluation/benchmarks/Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
reason: Proposes a new methodology to measure and interpret AI capabilities—the 50%-task-completion time horizon—providing a human-relative benchmark for evaluating model performance on long software tasks.
summary: AI's 50%-task-completion time horizon on software tasks reaches ~110 minutes for frontier models and doubles every 7 months since 2019, driven primarily by reliability, error recovery, reasoning, and tool use.

paper: llm/evaluation/methods/Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
reason: HELM is a comprehensive benchmarking system for language models, introducing datasets, scenarios, and metrics for standardized LM evaluation.
summary: HELM benchmarks 30 language models across 7 metrics and 42 scenarios, improving standardized evaluation coverage from 17.9% to 96.0% and exposing model-metric trade-offs.

paper: llm/foundation-models/NVIDIA Nemotron 3. Efficient and Open Intelligence
reason: Technical report introducing a new foundation model family with novel hybrid architecture and post-training approach.
summary: Nemotron 3: hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE models with 1M-token context and multi-environment RL post-training achieve strong reasoning and multi-step tool use.

paper: llm/personalization/benchmarks/LaMP. When Large Language Models Meet Personalization
reason: LaMP is a benchmark for training and evaluating personalized LLMs—the primary contribution fits the benchmarks folder under personalization rather than general LLM evaluation.
summary: A 7-task personalization benchmark (3 classification, 4 generation) shows retrieval augmentation of user profiles improves LLM outputs in zero-shot and fine-tuned settings.

paper: llm/personalization/methods/A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
reason: A roadmap for aligning models to pluralistic values through post-training methods and benchmarks.
summary: Alignment to pluralistic values defined through three operationalizations (Overton, steerable, distributional) and corresponding benchmarks; standard alignment reduces distributional pluralism.

paper: llm/personalization/user-modelling/RecToM. A Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Theory of Mind in LLM-based Conversational Recommender
reason: The paper evaluates Theory of Mind capabilities—inferring user mental states and using them to predict appropriate conversational actions—which is central to user modelling in recommendation dialogues.
summary: RecToM evaluates Theory of Mind in conversational recommenders through cognitive inference of user mental states and behavioral prediction of dialogue strategies; models struggle to maintain coherent, strategic reasoning in dynamic dialogues despite partial mental state recognition.

paper: llm/post-training/Large Language Model Post-Training. A Unified View of Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning
reason: Comprehensive survey unifying all major post-training methods (SFT, preference optimization, RL, distillation) under a single behavioral framework.
summary: Post-training methods unify under trajectory provenance (off-policy vs on-policy learning) and three behavioral roles: support expansion, policy reshaping, and behavioral consolidation.

paper: llm/post-training/data/Nemotron-4 340B Technical Report
reason: Technical report for a new model family release, though synthetic data for alignment is also a notable contribution.
summary: Nemotron-4 340B achieves competitive performance with over 98% synthetically generated data for alignment and fits on a single DGX H100.

paper: llm/post-training/fine-tuning/LoRA. Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
reason: LoRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method explicitly mentioned in this folder's scope.
summary: Injecting trainable rank decomposition matrices into frozen Transformer layers reduces trainable parameters by 10,000× and GPU memory by 3× versus full fine-tuning, while matching or exceeding fine-tuning performance on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3.

paper: llm/post-training/preference-learning/Unpacking DPO and PPO. Disentangling Best Practices for Learning from Preference Feedback
reason: Systematic study of DPO and PPO algorithms with preference data and reward models, fitting directly within preference-optimization methods.
summary: PPO outperforms DPO by up to 2.5% in math, with high-quality preference data driving improvements up to 8% in instruction following and truthfulness.

paper: llm/post-training/rl-for-reasoning/Beyond the 80 20 Rule. High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM
reason: Directly analyzes RLVR mechanisms through token entropy patterns to optimize reasoning performance on Qwen3 models.
summary: High-entropy minority tokens drive RLVR effectiveness: restricting policy gradients to these forking tokens (20% of total) maintains full-gradient performance on Qwen3-8B and achieves stronger scaling on larger models, with +11.04 on AIME'25 for Qwen3-32B.

paper: llm/routing/Adaptive-RAG. Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question
reason: Paper proposes adaptive selection of retrieval strategies for RAG systems based on query complexity, which is core to retrieval-augmented generation architecture and methods.
summary: A complexity classifier dynamically selects retrieval strategies (from no-retrieval to iterative) for each query, improving retrieval-augmented QA accuracy and efficiency over fixed-strategy and other adaptive baselines.

paper: llm/uncertainty-and-hallucination/DoLa. Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
reason: Directly addresses hallucination reduction and factuality improvement through a layer-based mechanism for surfacing correct knowledge.
summary: Decoding by contrasting later and earlier transformer layers improves LLaMA family models' truthfulness by 12-17 absolute points on TruthfulQA by surfacing factual knowledge localized to deeper layers.

paper: ml-foundations/classical-ml/An Introduction to Locally Linear Embedding
reason: LLE is a foundational unsupervised dimensionality reduction technique from the classical ML era, fitting the scope of classical methods before deep learning.
summary: Locally linear embedding computes low-dimensional neighborhood-preserving embeddings by exploiting local linear reconstructions, with optimization free of local minima.

paper: ml-foundations/evaluation-and-model-selection/Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
reason: Methodological paper on hyperparameter optimization strategies applied to neural networks and deep belief networks; folder explicitly covers hyperparameter-related topics alongside optimizers and schedules.
summary: Random search outperforms grid search for hyperparameter optimization, finding equal or better neural network configurations with substantially lower computational cost, while revealing that different hyperparameters are important for different datasets.

paper: ml-foundations/tabular/TabPFN. A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
reason: The paper applies a Transformer architecture to small tabular classification, comparing against GBDT and AutoML systems—fitting the folder's scope of tabular learning methods including tabular transformers and foundation models.
summary: Prior-Data Fitted Transformer for in-context learning outperforms boosted trees and matches AutoML on small tabular classification with 230× speedup.

paper: ml-systems/distributed-training/Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks
reason: Foundational paper on distributed training algorithms and systems for scaling deep networks across clusters.
summary: DistBelief's Downpour SGD and Sandblaster algorithms enable training deep networks across thousands of machines, achieving 30× larger models than prior work with state-of-the-art ImageNet performance.

paper: ml-systems/inference-and-serving/FlexGen. High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
reason: Presents an inference engine that optimizes LLM throughput through batching, KV cache compression, and efficient tensor storage on limited hardware.
summary: FlexGen achieves 1 token/s throughput for OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU through flexible memory aggregation from GPU/CPU/disk, LP-optimized tensor storage patterns, and 4-bit quantization of weights and attention.

paper: ml-systems/production-ml/Model Cards for Model Reporting
reason: The paper's core contribution is a framework for systematically documenting and evaluating model performance across demographic and intersectional groups, directly addressing fairness and bias assessment in ML systems.
summary: Model cards document trained models with performance evaluation across demographic and intersectional groups to surface disparities and guide responsible deployment.

paper: nlp/generation-metrics/MAUVE. Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers
reason: MAUVE is an automatic metric for evaluating generated text quality, comparable to BLEU and BERTScore which are explicitly listed in this folder's scope.
summary: MAUVE compares machine-generated and human text distributions using divergence frontiers in quantized embedding space, correlating with human judgments while requiring fewer restrictions than existing distributional metrics.

paper: nlp/pretrained-language-models/Revisiting Few-sample BERT Fine-tuning
reason: BERT-specific study of fine-tuning stability; the folder explicitly covers BERT-era encoders and fine-tuning them.
summary: Alternative optimization practices resolve few-sample BERT fine-tuning instability from biased gradient estimation and limited layer applicability, reducing the effectiveness of specialized methods.

paper: nlp/tasks-and-methods/Bad Characters. Imperceptible NLP Attacks
reason: Adversarial attacks threatening deployed NLP systems and language models
summary: Imperceptible character-level perturbations—invisible characters, homoglyphs, reordering, deletions—break deployed NLP systems in black-box attacks, with three injections functionally disabling most models.

paper: recommender-systems/collaborative-filtering/BPR. Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
reason: BPR is a ranking optimization criterion applied to matrix factorization and adaptive k-NN, core collaborative filtering models.
summary: BPR optimizes personalized ranking through Bayesian inference and bootstrap-sampled SGD, outperforming standard optimization of matrix factorization and adaptive k-NN.

paper: recommender-systems/deep-and-sequential/DeepFM. A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
reason: Deep neural network architecture for CTR prediction in recommender systems, improving on Wide & Deep with shared inputs and reduced feature engineering.
summary: DeepFM combines factorization machines with deep learning to capture low- and high-order feature interactions for CTR prediction without feature engineering.

paper: reinforcement-learning/world-models/Diffusion for World Modeling. Visual Details Matter in Atari
reason: The paper's core contribution is world models for RL, specifically using diffusion as the environment dynamics model instead of discrete latents.
summary: Using diffusion instead of discrete latents for world models preserves visual details crucial for RL, achieving 1.46 human-normalized score on Atari 100k—new best for agents trained in world models.

paper: representation-learning/embeddings/ArcFace. Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition
reason: Face recognition is a core computer vision task that should be organized with other vision applications like detection and segmentation.
summary: Angular margin loss (ArcFace) improves face recognition discriminative power with clear geometric interpretation; sub-center variant uses K sub-centers per class to separate clean and noisy samples.

paper: research-practice/Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers. A large-scale empirical
reason: Empirical study evaluating LLM-generated feedback through human evaluation (comparison with peer reviewers and user studies).
summary: GPT-4's generated feedback on research papers overlaps with human peer reviewers at 31% (Nature) and 39% (ICLR)—comparable to inter-reviewer agreement—and 57% of users find it helpful, though the model struggles with in-depth method critique.

paper: robotics-and-embodied/Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
reason: Robot manipulation learning from bimanual imitation with low-cost hardware.
summary: Action Chunking with Transformers learns fine-grained bimanual manipulation from 10 minutes of demonstrations on sub-$20k hardware, achieving 80-90% success on assembly tasks like battery slotting.

paper: search-and-ranking/ads/Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
reason: Directly addresses CTR prediction at scale, a core computational advertising problem.
summary: Decision trees combined with logistic regression improve Facebook ad click prediction by over 3%, with historical user and ad features proving dominant.

paper: search-and-ranking/click-models-and-unbiased-ltr/Unbiased Learning to Rank Meets Reality. Lessons from Baidu's Large-Scale Search Dataset
reason: The paper empirically evaluates unbiased learning-to-rank on real click data from a deployed search engine, directly addressing position bias and learning from user behaviour.
summary: Unbiased learning-to-rank robustly improves click prediction on Baidu's data but inconsistently improves ranking performance against expert annotations, with improvements dependent on evaluation metric choice.

paper: search-and-ranking/evaluation/Information Retrieval System Evaluation. Effort, Sensitivity, and Reliability
reason: Paper focuses on significance testing methodology, test collections, and IR evaluation metrics—core topics of IR evaluation.
summary: T-test outperforms sign and Wilcoxon tests for comparing IR systems; assessor effort is better allocated to building test collections with more topics, each assessed in less detail.

paper: search-and-ranking/indexing-and-classical-ir/SIMD Compression and the Intersection of Sorted Integers
reason: Covers inverted-index compression using SIMD and optimizing posting-list intersection, both core classical IR techniques.
summary: S4-BP128-D4 achieves 0.7 CPU cycles per decoded 32-bit integer; vectorized Galloping search with SIMD instructions doubles the speed of posting-list intersection for conjunctive queries.

paper: search-and-ranking/learning-to-rank/Accuracy at the Top
reason: Proposes a ranking algorithm with convex-surrogate loss for optimizing top-τ quantile accuracy, a learning-to-rank objective.
summary: A convex-surrogate algorithm for top τ-quantile accuracy achieves higher precision at the top than other high-precision ranking methods.

paper: search-and-ranking/neural-ranking/Pretrained Transformers for Text Ranking. BERT and Beyond
reason: Comprehensive survey of transformer-based text ranking covering both reranking and dense retrieval; BERT is explicitly mentioned in the neural-ranking scope and is the title's primary focus
summary: Transformer-based text ranking combines reranking in multi-stage architectures using relevance models and expansion methods with dense retrieval via learned representations, addressing challenges of long-document handling and effectiveness-efficiency tradeoffs.

paper: search-and-ranking/search-systems/Beyond Ranking. Optimizing Whole-Page Presentation
reason: Directly addresses whole-page presentation for heterogeneous search results, explicitly in scope of this folder.
summary: A framework learns content-aware page presentations for heterogeneous search results that outperform federated search algorithms.

paper: trustworthy-ml/ai-safety/AI Control. Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
reason: Develops safety protocols preventing code backdoors from untrusted models, robust to intentional subversion
summary: Trusted editing and monitoring protocols prevent code backdoors despite untrusted models' intentional subversion attempts.

paper: vision-and-multimodal/vision/Mask R-CNN
reason: Instance segmentation architecture for object detection and recognition tasks, fitting core vision detection and segmentation scope.
summary: A parallel mask prediction branch extends Faster R-CNN for instance segmentation and human pose estimation.
